samples.question: This image shows five framed rectangular panels of identical size standing side by side in one row, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Every panel contains exactly the same four things in the same colours: one small filled circle near the top, which is a point lamp; one straight solid tilted bar hanging below the lamp, which is opaque; and one thin horizontal grey rail near the bottom, which is the floor, with one thick coloured segment lying on that rail, which is the gateway. Colour and object count are the same in all five panels and carry no information, and no panel is marked out by how much ink it carries. The lamp shines from its own single point, so the bar throws a shadow onto the floor rail: the shadow of the bar covers exactly the part of the rail that is hit by straight lines drawn from the lamp point through the bar, which is the same as projecting the bar away from the lamp until it reaches the rail. That shadow is never drawn, and no line from the lamp is drawn; it has to be worked out from where the lamp, the bar and the rail are. In exactly one panel the whole shadow of the bar lands inside the coloured gateway segment, clear of both of its ends by at least 11 pixels. In each of the other four panels the shadow runs past an end of the gateway by at least 12 pixels, or misses the gateway altogether. The bar's own left-right position is not the shadow: in two of the losing panels the bar itself hangs directly above the gateway while its shadow still falls outside, and in the winning panel the bar does not hang above the gateway. Only the lamp centre, the bar and the gateway ends matter, and the tilt and length of the bar, the width of the gateway and the height of the rail carry no information. Which numbered panel is the one where the bar's whole shadow lands inside the coloured gateway segment? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.
